|--------|--------|--------|
| LeewayHertz | Custom LLM engineering | RAG, agents, knowledge assistants |
| IBM Consulting | Enterprise architecture | Hybrid cloud, governance, complex integrations |
| Slalom | Cloud and data integration | Internal copilots and business applications |
| EPAM Systems | Software engineering | Complex, production-grade AI products |
| Accenture | Transformation at scale | Multi-department AI deployment |
| HatchWorks AI | AI and data modernization | RAG and data-intensive applications |
| Booz Allen Hamilton | Security-sensitive delivery | Government and regulated environments |
| Markovate | Focused AI development | Custom AI features and automation |


## What matters most when choosing an enterprise LLM development partner

A vendor may demonstrate an impressive chatbot but still lack the engineering practices required for a reliable enterprise system. I would assess candidates against these six criteria.

**1\. RAG and enterprise data integration**

Can the team connect SharePoint, Confluence, Salesforce, internal databases, PDFs, and other data sources while preserving document-level permissions and access controls?

---

**2\. Security and governance**

Look for SSO, role-based access control, encryption, audit logs, sensitive-data handling, and documented data-retention policies. Require evidence for any claimed certifications.

---

**3\. Evaluation and reliability**

Ask how the team measures retrieval accuracy, grounded answers, hallucinations, latency, cost per request, and regression performance before and after releases.

---

**4\. Production architecture**

Confirm experience with model routing, vector or hybrid search, caching, monitoring, versioning, fallback behavior, and human approval for sensitive actions.

---

**5\. Deployment flexibility**

Establish whether the application can run in your AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud environment, and whether you can switch model providers without rebuilding the entire product.

---

**6\. Ownership and ongoing support**

Ensure you retain ownership of application code, prompts, evaluation datasets, infrastructure configuration, and relevant intellectual property. Agree on support SLAs and knowledge transfer.

## My recommendation by project type

- **Building one custom LLM application\:** Start with LeewayHertz, HatchWorks AI, and Markovate.
- **Building a large enterprise platform\:** Compare IBM Consulting, EPAM Systems, and Slalom.
- **Rolling out AI across an entire organization\:** Consider Accenture alongside IBM Consulting.
- **Handling highly sensitive or government data\:** Evaluate Booz Allen Hamilton and IBM Consulting against your specific compliance and deployment requirements.

## What matters most when choosing an enterprise LLM development partner

A vendor may demonstrate an impressive chatbot but still lack the engineering practices required for a reliable enterprise system. I would assess candidates against these six criteria.

**1\. RAG and enterprise data integration**

Can the team connect SharePoint, Confluence, Salesforce, internal databases, PDFs, and other data sources while preserving document-level permissions and access controls?

---

**2\. Security and governance**

Look for SSO, role-based access control, encryption, audit logs, sensitive-data handling, and documented data-retention policies. Require evidence for any claimed certifications.

---

**3\. Evaluation and reliability**

Ask how the team measures retrieval accuracy, grounded answers, hallucinations, latency, cost per request, and regression performance before and after releases.

---

**4\. Production architecture**

Confirm experience with model routing, vector or hybrid search, caching, monitoring, versioning, fallback behavior, and human approval for sensitive actions.

---

**5\. Deployment flexibility**

Establish whether the application can run in your AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud environment, and whether you can switch model providers without rebuilding the entire product.

---

**6\. Ownership and ongoing support**

Ensure you retain ownership of application code, prompts, evaluation datasets, infrastructure configuration, and relevant intellectual property. Agree on support SLAs and knowledge transfer.

## My recommendation by project type

- **Building one custom LLM application\:** Start with LeewayHertz, HatchWorks AI, and Markovate.
- **Building a large enterprise platform\:** Compare IBM Consulting, EPAM Systems, and Slalom.
- **Rolling out AI across an entire organization\:** Consider Accenture alongside IBM Consulting.
- **Handling highly sensitive or government data\:** Evaluate Booz Allen Hamilton and IBM Consulting against your specific compliance and deployment requirements.
